channel.title: Foundation for National Parks & Wildlife
channel.description: News and stories from our work growing national parks, saving species and healing the land.

item.title: The number almost no one publishes
item.description: A tree planted is not the same as a tree that lived. Why we have partnered with veritree to plant and verify 100,000 native trees across three landscapes.

item.title: The science of plant selection, and why the species matters
item.description: Put a Glossy Black-Cockatoo in a healthy forest and it can still starve. Why species list, seed source and genetic spread decide whether a planting works.

item.title: What does healthy bushland actually look like?
item.description: Researchers added 2,000 tonnes of dead wood at Mulligans Flat and found more reptiles nine years on. Why structure decides whether a planting is habitat.

item.title: Caring for Country Starts with Listening
item.description: Our partnership with Kaurna Kardla on Kaurna Yarta begins before any planting does. Kaurna knowledge holders on reading Country and listening first.

item.title: A wildlife corridor is only as wide as its narrowest point
item.description: Urban sprawl rarely wipes out a wildlife corridor outright, it pinches it. Four fast-growing regions show what width, continuity and permanence decide.

item.title: Your Backyard Is Habitat Too: Help Native Wildlife
item.description: Most of the green on a city map is mown lawn native animals cannot use. A backyard, courtyard or balcony planted with local natives becomes a safe step.

item.title: Years of restoration, written in layers
item.description: A morning in Hindmarsh Valley National Park, where a cleared paddock is becoming forest again, and why connection matters more than tree counts.

item.title: A million reasons to say thank you
item.description: One million trees in the ground, a strategy that is delivering and partnerships built to last. David Knowles reflects on eight years with our Foundation.

item.title: From advocate to chair: nature, ambition, and what comes next
item.description: Kelly O'Shanassy, who led the Australian Conservation Foundation for nearly 12 years, is our new President and Chair. She talks business and climate.

item.title: Caring for Country in Practice with Firesticks
item.description: At Field River in Hallett Cove, the Kaurna Firesticks team cares for Country with Cultural Fire, weed control and restoration, and we support that work.

item.title: Bringing Back the Growling Grass Frog
item.description: At Winton Wetlands in north-east Victoria, a founding population of 60 to 65 Growling Grass Frogs is in place, with monitoring to see whether they breed.

item.title: The Land Behind Australia's World Heritage Bid
item.description: Balcoracana Paddock, 4,500 hectares on Adnyamathanha Country, joins Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park, protecting fossil beds behind the Heritage bid.

item.title: Why Expanding National Parks Matters for Australia’s Future
item.description: Australia's ecosystems are broken into smaller pieces, and wildlife pays the price. Adding land to the national park estate reconnects those fragments.

item.title: Growing Resilience from the Ground Up
item.description: Restoration begins with seed, and Australia is short of it. Through our Landscape Resilience Program we back Trees For Life to collect and grow it.

item.title: A New Future for Mundoo Island and the Coorong
item.description: We helped secure Mundoo Island Station, a 1,900-hectare property at the Murray Mouth, bringing Ewe Island, Long Island and more into Coorong National Park.

item.title: The Importance of Wildlife Corridors This Summer
item.description: Connected habitat lets native animals find shade, water and a way out of a fire through Australia's hottest months. How a yard or balcony can help.

item.title: Lesser-Known Endangered Animals, and Why They Matter
item.description: Eight endangered Australian animals that rarely make headlines, from the yellow-bellied glider to the woylie, and what each does for its landscape.

item.title: Planning for Fire Season Starts in the Garden
item.description: Bushfire preparation is not only about clearing. Native plants, sensible spacing and connected neighbours make a place safer. What to do at home.

item.title: The Battle in the Treetops: Feathers, Flowers and a Fight for Survival
item.description: As eucalypt forests are cleared, fragmented or weakened by fire and drought, nectar-feeding birds are squeezed together and neighbours become rivals.

item.title: The Bandicoot: A Little Gardener Beneath Our Feet
item.description: One southern brown bandicoot turns close to four tonnes of soil a year. Why this shy digger matters, and how the Bandicoot Superhighway helps it.
